verdicts.note: The defect and the 0-byte canary move stand. KSIG_OFF only reaches `mov si, KSIG_OFF` in .boot2 and the Makefile's KSIGDEF2 (Makefile:1021, 1057). The packed kernel.sys is long enough at offset 22528: kern_small's file is 54224 bytes against 22528+5632+512. The -41 for boot-7 also re-sums from the encodings at boot2.asm:267-288 (1+1+2+2+4+3+5+3+1+2+5+3+3+1+2+1+1+1). Three things need amending. (1) KZIP is the shipped default (Makefile:1394-1395). On every shipped disk the splash-before-canary fix is therefore the KZ head loop (boot2.asm:336-345), not the SPL_RESIDENT tick gate at 360-365. The naive form moves the widening block (boot2.asm:298-316) to after `.head_next`. That breaks .rerun's one-shot guarantee (boot2.asm:524-533): .rerun sets runmax to spt and jumps to .reload, which would widen again after the head, and the canary would then loop for ever on exactly the BIOS it exists for. A safe form needs no guard: `mov ax,[b2_spt]` / `xchg ax,[b2_runmax]` / `push ax` before the head loop, then `pop word [b2_runmax]` after it. That is 12 bytes. .rerun's SP reset (boot2.asm:533) makes the push harmless on the error path. A self-patching guard could reach +5..+8. (2) Room: the +12 is needed only on kern_big. Its blob is 0x19FC of 0x1A00, so 4 bytes are free (kernel.map:14, 415), and there it needs boot-7's -41. kern_small has 702 bytes free (smallk map: 0x1342 of 0x1600) and kern_mega 285 (0x1AE3 of 0x1C00). (3) The latency was left out and should be stated. A track-bounded 9-sector head (kernel.kz.json headsecs 9) costs one extra int 13h, about 170-200 ms (one revolution at 300/360 rpm), on every 8088 boot where the head crosses a head. Those disks are kern_small 360/720 (head LBA 23..31), kern_big 1.2MB, and kern_big 1.44MB too (head LBA 46..54, which crosses at 54). It costs 0 on kern_big 360/720 and 0 on a 286+ that is not asked, which is already track-bounded (boot2.asm:311). ABI: none, correct.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: 0 resident; .boot2 +12 (safe xchg/push/pop form; +5..+8 only with a self-patching rerun guard), and kern_big needs boot-7's -41 for it; kern_small and kern_mega have room. Plus ~1 int 13h (~170-200 ms) per 8088 boot on 4 of 6 shipped system disks.

verdicts.note: vga12.inc:1886-1889 is `or cx,cx / jz vga_b4out / or dx,dx / jz vga_b4out`, two short backward jumps to vga_b4out at 1714. `jle` (7E) has the same 2-byte encoding as `jz` (74) and the same timing on an 8088 (16 taken / 4 not taken). After `or` OF is 0, so jle means ZF or SF: it refuses zero and negative, and accepts any width up to 32767, which covers every real screen. So the fix is 0 bytes and 0 cycles in .text on every kernel, gfx_blit4 being shared .text code. The optional gfx_blit1_x change (vga12.inc:5915, in .cold, section at 5870) turns `jcxz .refuse` (2) into `or cx,cx / jle .refuse` (4): +2 .cold, as stated. Its DX is already range-checked by the dec/cmp 0FFh/jae at 5916-5919. No cell or contract moves: OSAPI_GFX_BLIT4 (os88api.inc:1964) gives no sign semantics, so refusing a negative width is not an ABI event.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: 0 (+2 .cold for gfx_blit1_x's jcxz)

verdicts.note: The hazard and the fix shape stand, but the byte range has the wrong sign: the windowed path SAVES bytes. inst_task_die (instance.inc:1929-1953, .text on kern_big, kernel.map:5162 linear 80AD / offset 66AD) loses gfx_lock, `mov bx,[di+I_WIN]`, inst_unwin, the far desk_drop_x, gfx_unlock, mem_free_rec and `mov bx,di`: 3+3+3+5+3+3+2 = 22 bytes. Its inst_rel_rec and toast_owner_gone can go too (-6), because the task-less arm repeats inst_rel_rec, inst_unwin, mem_free_rec, desk_drop_x and the release (instance.inc:1713-1738). The posting already exists: wm_close_req (wm.inc:2236-2246) sets the slot bit and ui_post, and ui.inc:875-900's .cl_slot retires the negotiator and calls app_close_win. The adds are `mov byte [di+I_TASK],0FFh` (4), `mov bx,[di+I_WIN]` / `call wm_close_req` (6) and `xor bx,bx` before task_exit (2): about +12 against -22..-28. The only positive part is the windowless record (inst_pkg_alive's winless leg, instance.inc:842), which needs a reap byte (+1 .bss), a UI-pass test (~7 .text, on the idle path, ~20 clocks a pass) and a handler of about 20 bytes (unwin with BX=0, mem_free_rec, desk_drop, release, under the lock). That gives -15 for the windowed path alone and about +15 with the reap. The savings come out of .text and relieve KERN_CODE_MAX as well as KERN_BUDGET. Ordering cost: I_TASK=0xFF and the post must go inside task_exit's IF=0 window (`cli`, +1), so the UI pass cannot free the record while the worker still runs on it. Latency: the close completes on the next UI pass, which is negligible. hm-3's separate +8..+12 is subsumed, since the drop now runs on the UI task, which cannot also be inside dkd_hover. ABI: none.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: net -15..+16 resident (.text savings in inst_task_die; positive only for the windowless reap: +1 .bss, ~+27 .text/.cold)

verdicts.note: The mechanism stands. drv_wcnt is one byte (driver.inc:6132; the item cites 6139). The global counter moves at three sites (spawn, refused spawn, exit; driver.inc:4592, 4609, 4617). The unload wait is at 4163-4182 and the pin test at memory.inc:2143. drv_unload_x is .cold (kernel.map:9601, linear 18FD3 / offset F0F3, with mem_shed_one's .cold delta). The code estimate of about +25 .cold is realistic. Each of the three sites needs a row index: at spawn and exit drv_row_ix_of / drv_owns_seg_x already do the drv_tab walk (driver.inc:2014-2020), at about +3..+5 each with register banking. The unload's two compares need an index register beside BX's row pointer (+3..+5). The pin test needs the image-to-row map (+5), and the timeout unpublish needs +5..+10. Total about +20..+35 .cold. On kern_mega .cold goes above 1MB, so it is not MEGA_RESIDENT there. The table cannot ride in drv_tab: DRVR_SIZE is a full 16 bytes (driver.inc:249-270), so it needs a separate .bss table. The .bss figure is right for kern_big and kern_mega: DRV_MAX is 11 on both (kernel.map and megak map: DRV_VX 1, DRV_PX 1, DRV_MAX 0Bh). It is wrong for kern_emu: DRV_MAX equ 10 + DRV_VX + DRV_PX (driver.inc:63) gives 12. The figure is +11/+12 if the global byte is kept for K1a's MC_DMA pin, or one less if the table replaces it. .bss is conventional and resident on every kernel, mega included. ABI: none. Neither DRVV_DETACH nor the worker-spawn contract in drivers/os88drv.inc changes.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: +20..+35 .cold; .bss +11 kern_big/mega, +12 kern_emu (each one less if the table replaces drv_wcnt); 0 kern_small

verdicts.note: The defect is real, the section (.boot2, transient, 0 resident) is right and ABI is none (no cell, contract or record moves). What is wrong is the byte figure on kern_big, plus a missing kernel. (1) On kern_big vid_memchk is in .ovl (build/kernel.map:6370, real 0xCE00, virtual 0), and vid_detect runs in the blob (viddet.inc:538-610, retf BLOBCALL). The verify note in data/video.json says the estimate 'assumes' a copy of vid_memchk in the blob, but that copy alone is 55 bytes (0xCE00..vid_probe_avail 0xCE37). On top of it come the 3BFh=1 write (6 bytes), the B000 and B800 probes with their branches (~14) and the MDA-alone halt with a message (~30-40), so +60..+110 .boot2, not +25..+35. The Wilton 3BAh toggle replaces only the MDA test (~20 bytes); the B800 probe still needs a memory test. (2) The blob ends at boot2_end 0x19FC against BOOT2_SECS 13 = 0x1A00 (kernel.asm:2111; map:3127): 4 bytes free. So a 14th blob sector is CERTAIN on kern_big, not 'may', even after WP6's boot-7 frees -41. Cheaper shape: move vid_memchk from .ovl into .boot2 on kern_big, as kern_small already has it. It is boot-only there, and it frees 55 bytes of an .ovl at 5,116/5,120. It still costs the sector. (3) kern_small: vid_memchk is already in .boot2 (smallk map:2034, 0x8E9), so +25..+35 holds for the probe, plus ~+30 if it halts with a message. 702 bytes free (0x1342 of 11*512). (4) kern_mega is omitted but runs the same vid_detect (megak map:2999) on 286+ machines, and an AT with an MDA primary is plausible. Its vid_memchk is also .ovl (megak 0xE600), so it pays the copy, but its blob has 285 bytes free (0x1AE3 of 14*512), so it fits. Latency: boot only. On kern_big, one more sector in the contiguous read costs ~+22 ms on a 360KB disk (200 ms/rev / 9 spt), and guard 5's boot footprint grows by +512.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: kern_big +60..+110 .boot2 (14th blob sector certain: 4 bytes free), or move vid_memchk .ovl->.boot2 (.ovl -55, blob +~85); kern_small +25..+65 .boot2 (fits, 702 free); kern_mega +60..+110 .boot2 (fits, 285 free); 0 resident on all; boot +~22 ms/+512 boot footprint on kern_big

verdicts.note: The holes are real and ABI is none: the header layout is unchanged, and os88pkg.py and cmz_hdr already refuse these files. The estimate is low for the design the synthesis recommends, and the 'resident, all kernels' label is wrong for kern_mega. (1) 'Compute the prefix once in ld_check_hdr and keep it in a .bss word' MOVES the ~31-byte ladder (loader.inc:1018-1035) rather than saving it. In ld_check_hdr the flags are in DL, and `test dl,imm8` is 3 bytes against `test al,imm8`'s 2, so +4. Storing and reloading the word adds ~+8 .cold and +2 .bss. The three bounds (image>prefix ~4-6, file>prefix ~6, R+file<=roundup512(image+bss) ~15, since R is computed only in ld_where at 878-885) are on top. That is ~+35..+45 .cold and +2 .bss. The in-place shape is cheaper: two cmp/jbe pairs at 1066-1067 plus a pop-ds LD_EBAD stub (+14, loader-1 standalone), the fit test in ld_where after `and bx,0FE00h` against [ld_need] (+12..16), and loader-2's `cmp dx,[ld_need]/ja` (+6, verified: DX = image+bss survives ld_check_hdr, 506-524). That totals ~+32..+36 .cold, 0 .bss. Either way it is ~+32..+45, not ~+24. (2) The section is right on kern_big and kern_small: ld_check_hdr is .cold at kernel.map:8304 (0x14CEA) and smallk 0xD82B. On kern_mega it is .cold at 0x17B09, inside a .cold that starts at 0x11000 and lives above 1MB, so it costs 0 MEGA_RESIDENT and the bytes are high. Only the optional .bss word would be conventional. Latency: a dozen instructions per launch (<100 clocks), against a load that costs ~400 ms per int 13h call. Nil.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: ~+32..+45 .cold (+0..+2 .bss) on kern_big and kern_small; kern_mega 0 conv (+0..+2 .bss) / +32..+45 high

verdicts.note: The primary fix stands. wm_ptr2idx is 19 bytes (kernel.map 0x51AE..wm_zabove 0x51C1). `cmp ax,MAX_WIN*WIN_SIZE` (3D iw, 3 bytes) plus jae (2) is +5. It can be +1..+2: once AX is bounded, AL < MAX_WIN always holds, so the post-div `cmp al,MAX_WIN / jb .ok` (wm.inc:7275-7276, 4 bytes) is redundant and the existing `mov al,MAX_WIN-1` becomes the jae target (a 1-byte SKIP over it, the 0xA9 idiom already used in this module). An alternative is `call wm_isrec / jae` (wm.inc:11655-11661, O(1)), the same 5 bytes. Clocks: +~8 execution, ~20 at the fetch floor, against an 80-90 clock div. The wm-2 alternative's '-8 .text +12 .bss = +4 / -2' omits the W_IDX fill. wm_create's zero run (wm.inc:1421-1423) cannot set it, so wm-2 puts it in wm_init. That is a ~10-15 byte loop in .boot2/.ovl, and on kern_big both are full (blob 4 bytes free, .ovl 5,116/5,120), so it competes with the BR-6/WP6 ledger. Corrected: kern_big +4 resident +10..15 transient, kern_small -2 resident +10..15 transient. ~-75 clocks per call stands. The wake fence (+6..+12 .text) is plausible: call wm_isrec + jae + exit. In ISR context it adds ~60-80 clocks, which is acceptable. ABI none is right: os88api.inc:4194 deliberately publishes no WIN_SIZE. wm-2 does move the host mirror tools/os88geom.py, which t_mirror checks (wm.inc:129-131), so name it in the fix's file list.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: +1..+5 .text resident (bounded compare, folding the now-redundant post-div clamp); or wm-2: +4 kern_big / -2 kern_small resident PLUS +10..15 in .boot2/.ovl for the W_IDX fill; wake fence +6..+12 .text

verdicts.note: The resident figure checks out. filecp .cold is fcp_arm 0x17010..fdlg_ref 0x17689 = 1,657 and fdlg .cold is 0x17689..desk_zs 0x17EA9 = 2,080 (build/kernel.map:8993/9115/9250). With .text/.bss that is ~3.95-4.0KB. -3,600 leaves ~350-400 resident for doors, consistent with kern_small's 295-byte resident halves. kern_big's module has MORE entries than kern_small's (fdlg's thumb-drag onup/ondrag, kernel.asm:1106-1108, and FM_MSEL, filecp.inc:498), so -3,600 is the realistic ceiling. The 'check MEM_PG_LOW first' question is answered: tests/kernresident.py:87-92 skips owners MEM_PG_MIN..MEM_PG_MAX, and MEM_PG_LOW = 0xFC lies in that range (memory.inc:355-359). Excluding kern_mega is correct: its fcp_arm is .cold at 0x19EDA, in a .cold based at 0x11000 above 1MB. ABI: none for the core. The optional hm-9 verb is an additive OSAPI_MEM_P cell, an abilock --update without a bump. What must change: (1) the cost lands somewhere that is not named. The images must ride in KERNEL.SYS's read and be copied at mem_unblob. That adds ~4KB unpacked to the boot-time transient footprint on the 128KB machine (guard 5 / MIN_RAM_KB, kernel.asm:1512), and the phase-1 text itself says boot space binds. The plan must say where they sit at boot. The blob is impossible (4 bytes free), so it is above KERN_END in the main read. (2) The boot time is understated. ~5-6 packed sectors is ~+130 ms on a contiguous 360KB read. Add the lz decode, and the copy at ~13.3 cycles a byte (kernel.asm:8763-8764, PERFORMANCE Set 117.2), ~11 ms for 4KB. A read that crosses a head or track adds up to a revolution, so +140..+350 ms, ESTIMATED. (3) The runtime cost is not priced. Every FDLG/FCP entry gains a mod thunk plus a pin inc/dec (~50-100 clocks), including fdlg_ondrag on each drag event. That is negligible against a redraw, but it should be stated. (4) After a shed, the reload is ~1-2 int 13h calls (~0.4-0.8 s) plus a possible disk swap on Save As, a path that today never touches the disk. That is the latency the refusal answers.
verdicts.corrected_bytes: kern_big -3,408..-3,492 resident stands (ceiling); +~4,000 boot-time transient on the 128KB boot (guard 5) not stated; boot +140..+350 ms (ESTIMATED) rather than ~+120; kern_small 0..+12; kern_mega 0 conv / +48..92 high

verdicts.note: Mostly holds. Measurements: kbm_tab 0x43E9..kbm_isr 0x455F = 374, less mou_clamp (0x451B..0x455F, 68) = 306 on kern_big. kern_small has the same 306 (0x3054..0x31A6 = 338, less mou_clamp 32). kbm_p5spend is 16 on both. The PS/2 run is 0x42EE..0x43E9 = 251. font_run_x.planar 0x3E65 and fnt_rn_edge's VGA arm 0x3F78..0x3FA3 (fnt_rn_edge.mono) match. Phase is right: KBMOUSE is a kernel module (mod.inc/os88mod.py), not the drivers/os88drv.inc ABI, and the AT rung is internal, so no ABI. The slide decision runs in .cfx, which is transient (kernel.asm:5753), so bytes-2 really is 0 on the gauge: the gauge machine os8088_xt_vga_128k (tests/kernresident.py:44) is an 8088 with VGA, which keeps the AT bytes under the [AT][VGA][COLD] layout. On kern_mega, kbm_* is .text (megak 0x4E24, conventional) and modules live high (mod.inc:907-919), so -300..-380 conv and 0 conv for the image both hold. Changes: (1) text-7's '+10 on the gauge' is low. 8086 conditional jumps are short-only, so each of the two doors into .vga is a jcc-over plus a near jmp (5 bytes .text), and each arm needs a jmp back (3 bytes .vga, which the VGA gauge counts). That is ~+16 on the gauge, and the mono saving is ~-177 (187 out, ~10 of doors left), not -185. The per-run VGA cost is two near jmps plus queue refills, ~30-40 clocks rather than ~15. That is still <1% of the ~4,300-cycle prologue. (2) input-12's retained resident part must also carry the new mod_tab row, a 4-byte .bss slot per entry (SPEC 2.8.1), the post-to-UI load path (the first press must not load in the ISR) and the mou_ptr drop that t_moddrop requires. The low end (-300) is the realistic one. KBMOUSE.DRV also takes a cluster on every system disk, small360 included. Corrected totals: kern_small -290..-360; kern_big -275..-350 on the gauge and -705..-855 on a mono XT; kern_mega -290..-360 conv.

verdicts.note: kern_big is about right; kern_small, kern_mega and drivers-13 are wrong. (1) kern_small: histsys-7 saves 0 there, not -36. drv_svc/drv_owner sit inside driver.inc's second OS88_DRIVERS gate (driver.inc:3389-6883; the first gate closes at 3387 for drvvol.inc). build/smallk/kernel.map has neither symbol; its .bss runs gfx_u..snd_inst with no drv_ rows. kern_small's WP4 is bytes-8 alone: 5 mod_f_* names (ctrl/fmt/dops/fcp/fdlg, smallk map 7A9B..7AD7), 20 bytes gross, about -10 net. (2) kern_big: drv_svc B0FE..B1FA = 252 bytes (map), so dropping 6 copies is -216 .bss. Add back +12..18 .bss for a per-class table offset and length, plus the length-tested reads behind ~14 drv_cls_svc_x callers. -90..-140 is plausible but unmeasured. drivers-10: drv_f_sound..drv_f_eth is AD9A..AE06 = 108 bytes of .text less fdlg_s_drive's 6 = 102, which matches '~100'. bytes-8 is about -25. So drivers-10 + bytes-8 is about -127; '-120' is fine. (3) kern_mega is NOT 'about the same'. drv_svc (C796..C892), drv_f_* (C458..) and mod_f_* (B42F..) are all conventional .bss/.text. But drv_cls_svc_x (1BADA) and its callers are .cold, which is high on mega. So the gain is about -320..-350 CONVENTIONAL (-216+14 .bss, -102 and -36 .text), against about +50..+110 HIGH (.cold read code and suffix staging). (4) drivers-13 is mis-costed and should be dropped or re-scoped. drv_svc_call_x is 38 bytes (18C63..18C89), not ~40/+36, and it near-calls wm_nest_pushd/wm_nest_pop, which are .cold (1062C/10658). From .text those become far calls, as drv_pkg_call_x already does (driver.inc:6636, 6643: call COLD_SEG:wm_nest_pushd_x / wm_nest_pop_x). Moving the body into .text therefore swaps one far round trip for two: about +8 bytes .text and +~60 cycles, not -4 bytes and a saving. Also, the '~300 cycles/~65 us' is the whole dispatch. The thunk hop itself (call far + retf + the thunk's ret) is about 90-110 cycles, about 20 us at 4.77 MHz. (5) ABI/phase stand. No layout or cell moves, so the os88drv.inc text edits are one --update with no bump. Note that removing 'PRESERVE BX' from the driver contract only relaxes drivers. A new BX-clobbering driver would break on an older kernel, which is harmless while drivers ship on the system disk with their kernel; say so in the abilock reason. Corrected: kern_big -200..-260 (drivers-13 out); kern_small -10; kern_mega about -320..-350 conv and +50..+110 high; images +~100 each plus +2 (drivers-5).

The byte figures hold: md-6 357+189+459+23 = 1,028, md-7 512, md-13 40, md-14 8, so each kern_mega image is -1,588 and kern_big's is -560. What must change is the sentence 'every byte here is handed to the DOS program'. It is false for the default kern_mega arm and false at byte level on kern_big. (a) On the HMA arm the image is assembled at FFFF:0010. kdlayout.inc:24-29 and 140-142 say 'this rung no longer comes off the DOS program at all - it is the HMA's'. So 39,465 - 1,588 = 37,877 is HMA headroom (KD_IMG_KB 39 -> 37), with 0 conventional bytes to the program. (b) The LOW arm (KD_LOWDOS, kdlayout.inc:148-155) does go to the program, but only through the KIMG_PARA = KD_IMG_KB*64 rung (kdlayout.inc:162). 37,510 - 1,588 = 35,922 drops 37 -> 36 KB, +1 KB to the program. It does not reach 35 KB (35,840): it is 82 bytes over. (c) kern_big: 34,796 - 560 = 34,236, still inside rung 34 (34,816). The program gains nothing until another ~444 bytes go (33,792). The bytes are real per the banner, but that phrasing should go. Kernel side: md-8 is -11 .mega per its own finding (megados.md md-8), not -15. So high is -11-70+16 = -65, not -69, and -22 conv (md-19) stands. mc-16's -70 is an estimate (mega_i21 81 bytes per the map, less two mega_swv stubs; symbolising the 20h literals is assembly-time, 0 bytes). No item moves os88api.inc/os88drv.inc, so phase 1 is correct, apart from the optional md-15, which is the KDL_VER bump the WP already flags.

Sums check against the per-item figures: kern_big 14+19+7+3+1+3+6+2+3 = -58. kern_small 19+7+3+1+3+6+2+3+84 = -128. kern_mega conv = the .text items 14+19+7+3+1 = -44. kern_mega high = .cold 3+6+2+20 plus mc-11's 4 = -35. Placement checks out: font_ink (2143), ui_dispatch (7EA0), wm_lk (449E), vid_popmax (78F) and sch_clsbytes (3A94) are .text in all three maps, so 'conv' on mega is right; dsk_ico_stage and ld_unreserve are .cold (high on mega). video-7 measured: fsx_mtab is 89DE..8A5C = 126 bytes = 9 rows x 14 in build/smallk/kernel.map, so rows 5-8 are 56. bmodes ids 5-7 are 3, keeping id 8's byte per fsx.inc:1194-1203. The capstab VGA row is 2. fsx_page's Mode X arm (fsx.inc:1014-1028) encodes to about 27 bytes, less the 2-byte jne that replaces it. That is -84..-86, inside -82..-86. text-2's ~40 clocks per mono glyph is right for the cmp mem,imm + untaken jcc that font.inc:603-610 removes. drivers-12's -4 is .boot2 as stated. No ABI or record layout is touched.

The direction is right and no ABI moves: WIN_SIZE is unpublished (apps/os88api.inc:4194; only MAX_WIN is mirrored), and W_IDX goes at the record's end. But the growth is under-costed and two sections are wrong. (1) Stubs + panel: '+30' is optimistic. Each stub is 4-5 bytes (mov al/si + jmp short), 8-10 for two. The glue must pop the faulting IP/CS, load DS, and print two sch_dphex4 values with a ':' before reaching sch_diepanel's hang (sch_diepanel 53AF..5437 = 136 bytes today, kernel.map). The new message text is extra on top: sch_s_over alone is 22 bytes. Realistic: +40..+60 resident .text on kern_big and kern_small (mega .text too: sch_diepanel is conv 5F35). (2) Install: '+12 .ovl' is low. sched_init must store the segment as the constant KERNEL_SEG, not CS (sched.inc:296-304, os88ovlchk rule 2b). With ES=0, each `mov word [es:d16],imm16` is 7 bytes, so int 0 is 14 bytes and int 6 is 14 plus a cpu_tier test (~7). A stosw form is ~10 + ~18. So +20..+30. verdicts.note:
The idea and the flag-day phase hold. Three cost figures are wrong.

(1) kern_small is not -245. I decoded the tables in build/smallk/kernel-full.bin, build/kernel-full.bin and build/megak/kernel-full.bin (.text at file 0x1600 / 0x1A00 / 0x1C00; osapi_table 0x10..0x4FB in all three maps). kern_small has the same 112 rare cells as kern_big (RSLOT 51, RCSLOT 18, RXCELL 7, RCXCELL 24, RNCELL 12; 96 distinct targets, because the refusal cells share one). The same five kind bodies sit at the same offsets (api_rx 0x511 .. api_rn 0x55F). So the synthesis's own arithmetic (-672 +224 +door +tails +12) gives kern_small the same figure as kern_big. kern_mega has 119 rare cells (RSLOT 57), so its cell term is -714 +238, which is 28 bytes more than kern_big.

(2) The door is not ~45 bytes. A door that does all of the following is about 75-95 bytes:
- bank DS and SI, `lds si,[bp+2]`, `inc word [bp+2]`, mask the index byte;
- bounds-check the index, with a CF=1/AX=1 `retf 2` refusal tail of about 10 bytes;
- test the stacked IF (`test byte [bp+7],2`; `jz`; `sti`);
- `mov bp,[cs:tab+si]`, then 4 range compares and 5 `pop si / pop ds / jmp body` exits (pops preserve flags, but each exit needs its own pops).

The tails are not +6, and the bodies do not run "unchanged". api_rx falls through into api_x (kernel.asm:4588-4603), and api_rxc jumps to api_x.done (kernel.asm:4624). Every hot XCELL shares that body and its plain `retf`. So rare X needs its own copy of the body ending in `retf 2` (~13 bytes), plus `retf`->`retf 2` on api_rs.tail (+2, kernel.asm:4650-4653): about +15.

Corrected kernel figures: about -330 to -350 .text on kern_big AND on kern_small, and about -355 to -380 conventional on kern_mega. kern_mega already has a 256-entry IDT (mega.inc:87), so the gate costs only a few `.cold` bytes, above 1MB.

(3) Cycles: the door executes about 50 bytes of instructions. At the 8088 fetch floor (4.34 clocks/byte) that alone is about 220 clocks. Add int's 71 and subtract the ~105 it replaces (far call 36, push bp 15, near call 23, pop bp 12, `mov bp,[cs:bp]` ~19). Result: about +200 to +300 clocks a rare call, 42-63 us, PREDICTED. gfr-1's +150 to +215 is low by roughly 50-90 clocks. This sharpens V7: OSAPI_SEG and FS_OP must be read before they are left rare. A rare call also holds 2 more stack bytes (the FLAGS word) for the body's whole life, and IRQs stay off for about 100 clocks until the conditional `sti`.

Packages: my naive census gives 2,641 rare `call` sites out of 6,998 (111 rare SDK `%define`s), against the synthesis's 2,736. So -2 a site is about -5.3 to -5.5KB unpacked; keep the figure. Phase: flag day (PKG_FMT and DRV_VER both bump), correct.

verdicts.note:
The pads are measured correctly. .bss ends at 0xB27E, 0x80CB and 0xC918, and KIMG_PARA (kernel.asm:1668) rounds them to 0xB400, 0x8200 and 0xCA00. FAT_SEG = KERNEL_SEG + KIMG_PARA is at kernel.asm:1804. The row does need the flag day: KERNEL_SEG moves.

What is wrong is quoting the pad as the resident saving. Once the image is paragraph-rounded rather than 512-rounded, the ladder-sum saving is -384 / -304 / -224 bytes. What it realizes depends on the ladder rule that remains.

kern_big and kern_small build LADDER_PACK (kernel.asm:1172-1176), so KERN_END is the one rounding (kernel.asm:1904). I recomputed both maps' ladders with dsk_secbuf (`.lowbss` offset 0) moved below along with the FAT:
- kern_big: KERN_END 0x1800 -> 0x17E0, so KERN_SIZE falls 512 today.
- kern_small: 0xEB7 -> 0xEA4, which still rounds to 0xEC0, so KERN_SIZE falls 0 today. The 304 bytes become slack under the one rounding.

kern_mega has no ROM_ADOPT, so no LADDER_PACK (kernel.asm:1142-1146). Every rung there is 512-rounded (LOW_PARA at kernel.asm:1816), COLD_SEG is a multiple of 8 paragraphs, and the post-switch heap floor must stay 512-aligned. Its COLD_RAM goes 0xFA0 -> 0xF92, which re-aligns to 0xFA0. So kern_mega's conventional saving is a STRUCTURAL 0, not rung luck. It becomes real only if the row also packs kern_mega's ladder, which is the measurement ABI-BREAK-LIST's own L1 note asked for.
